page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Small fragments of marginal text stand at the left edge, cut off by the scan. The right edge shows the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: drachmas, deferunto ad senatum, aut prima concione in curia. Ubi autem citationes recensuerint, judicanto: quòd si condemnatus, clam suffragia ferentibus senatoribus, praesides exactoribus legum eum inscribunto. Hactenus verba novæ legis.

In eadem Timarchea ab Æschine memoratur lex à Solone quondam scripta de disciplinâ matronarum, cujus hæc sententia: Mulierem apud quam adulter fuerit deprehensus, ornari vetat, ac in fana publica ingredi, ne suo interventu integras matronas corrumpat.

Quòd si intraverit, aut se ornaverit, quamvis vestimenta ejus dilacerare, ac ornatum diripere jubet, verberibusque eam excipere, veruntamen citra eadem ac mutilationem. Hac ratione, ait Æschines, mulierem talem omni dignitate privat, & vitam ipsa morte acerbiorem ei reddit. [illegible, ~3 letters]Lenones item accusari Solon jubet, & convicios capite plecti; propterea quod mercede locata sua impudentia iis, qui delinquere quidem cupiunt, attamen colloqui inter se verentur, efficere solent, ut periculum faciant, & colloquantur. page.notes: Left margin: only cut-off fragments survive (e.g. near "Lenones" and the lines below), too damaged to read; marked illegible. Right margin: the neighbouring page's text and edge, not transcribed. Below the text at the lower left, faint marks ("II.", "fed b.", "ieq pɔr t") appear to be show-through or the neighbouring page and are left out. The catchword "quam" is taken from the foot of the page. Printed spelling kept: "convicios" was read as printed, with some doubt.
